title: The Heart of the Heart Nebula
caption: The open cluster IC 1805 in the Heart Nebula, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This view from Kitt Peak looks into the middle of the Heart Nebula, a sprawling cloud of glowing gas that is informally named for its overall shape. The frame shows only the inner part of the cloud, where a young star cluster called IC 1805 sits.

The Heart is an emission nebula, which means its gas shines on its own. Hot young stars like the ones in IC 1805 pour out ultraviolet light, and that light strips electrons from the surrounding hydrogen. When the atoms recapture them, they give off a deep red glow, the color that dominates pictures of nebulae like this one.

An open cluster is a loose family of stars that formed together from the same cloud. Over time its members drift apart, but for now the cluster is still wrapped in the gas it was born from, and its light is shaping that gas from the inside.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on Kitt Peak's Mayall 4-meter Telescope combined three filters: hydrogen-alpha shown in red, near-infrared I band in orange, and blue B band in blue.
filters: 436 nm · Optical B (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)

understand.eye: The I-band light is just beyond what the eye can see, and the nebula is far too faint to show its color without a long camera exposure.

explore: The picture was made with the wide-field Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory. North is up and east is to the left. The Heart Nebula is also cataloged under the name of its cluster, IC 1805.
alt: Red glowing gas around a scattering of young stars at the center of the Heart Nebula.
